facts.statement: Plesiosuchus was a geosaurine metriorhynchid crocodyliform that lived during the Late Jurassic in England and possibly Spain.
facts.quote: Plesiosuchus is an extinct genus of geosaurine metriorhynchid crocodyliform known from the Late Jurassic (late Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian stage) of Dorset, England and possibly also Spain.

facts.statement: John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell discovered the type and referred specimens of Plesiosuchus in the 1860s along the coast of Dorset.
facts.quote: The type and referred specimens of Plesiosuchus were discovered by John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell in the 1860s alongside the remains of several other large-bodied marine reptiles along the coast of Dorset.

facts.statement: Richard Owen established the genus Plesiosuchus in 1884 because he believed the species was more similar to modern crocodilians than to Steneosaurus.
facts.quote: Richard Owen erected the genus Plesiosuchus for S. manselii in 1884 as he considered it to be more similar morphologically to extant crocodylians than to Steneosaurus.

facts.statement: The holotype of Plesiosuchus is estimated to have reached a total body length of 5.42 meters, though its age status remains uncertain.
facts.quote: The holotype of Plesiosuchus represents a large individual. Although it is uncertain whether the holotype (and referred specimens) belong to adults or subadults as none of the vertebrae are well enough preserved to determine the nature of the neurocentral sutures, its total body length is estimated to be 5.42 m.

facts.statement: A referred specimen of Plesiosuchus had a mandible measuring 132.2 cm, making it larger than the holotype which had a mandible of approximately 111 cm.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R1089 represents even larger individual than the holotype with 132.2 cm long mandible, while the mandible of NHMUK PV OR40103a is approximately 111 cm in length.

facts.statement: The largest known individual of Plesiosuchus is estimated to have been about 6.83 meters long, exceeding the estimated length of the pliosaur Liopleurodon ferox.
facts.quote: Thus, NHMUK PV R1089 has been estimated to have been about 6.83 m in length, surpassing the estimated length of the pliosaurid Liopleurodon ferox, which is approximately 6.39 m.

facts.statement: Researchers identified seven unique anatomical features in Plesiosuchus manselii that distinguish it from all other metriorhynchids.
facts.quote: Young et al. (2012) identified seven autapomorphies of P. manselii that this species possesses to the exclusion of all other metriorhynchids.

facts.statement: Plesiosuchus teeth featured rectangular-shaped denticles and inconspicuous enamel ornamentation with low-relief ridges aligned from tip to base.
facts.quote: P. manselii have rectangular-shaped denticles in lingual view. Its tooth enamel ornamentation is largely inconspicuous, but there are apicobasally aligned ridges of low-relief.

facts.statement: Plesiosuchus possessed large, robust teeth with moderate to strong side-to-side compression, a trait shared with other geosaurins.
facts.quote: Like other geosaurins, P. manselii have large robust teeth, with moderate to strong mediolateral compression.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses suggest that Plesiosuchus manselii and Dakosaurus maximus are actually separate species within the genus Dakosaurus.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses of Young & Andrade (2009), Cau & Fanti (2011) and Young et al. (2011) support the hypothesis that the two are separate species of Dakosaurus.

facts.statement: Young et al. (2012) revived the genus name Plesiosuchus after finding that Dakosaurus was paraphyletic and placing Plesiosuchus in a more basal position within Geosaurini.
facts.quote: Young et al. (2012) resurrected the genus name Plesiosuchus as their phylogenetic analysis found a paraphyletic Dakosaurus and suggested more basal position for P. manselii within Geosaurini than previously thought.

facts.statement: The holotype of Plesiosuchus was collected from the Lower Kimmeridge Clay Formation in Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset, dating to the late Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: It was collected from the late Kimmeridgian (Aulacostephanus autissiodorensis Sub-Boreal ammonite Zone) Lower Kimmeridge Clay Formation of Kimmeridge Bay, Dorset.

facts.statement: Fossil teeth attributed to Plesiosuchus were found in the Kimmeridgian-aged Tereñes Formation in Asturias, northern Spain.
facts.quote: It was collected from the Kimmeridgian-aged Tereñes Formation in La Griega Beach of Asturias, northern Spain.

facts.statement: A referred specimen of Plesiosuchus showed an extreme reduction in tooth sockets, having only 13 alveoli compared to 19–25 in the related genus Machimosaurus.
facts.quote: NHMUK PV R1089 exhibits extreme reduction in dentition (13 dentary alveoli compared to 19–25 in Machimosaurus) that is otherwise observed in geosaurine metriorhynchids.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Plesiosuchus manselii at the base of the Geosaurini tribe in a polytomy with Torvoneustes and a clade containing Dakosaurus and Geosaurus.
facts.quote: P. manselii was found in a polytomy at the base of Geosaurini with Torvoneustes and a clade that includes Dakosaurus and Geosaurus.

facts.statement: The closest known relative of the genus Plesiosuchus is the genus Suchodus.
facts.quote: The closest relative of Plesiosuchus is the genus Suchodus.

facts.statement: The type species, originally named Steneosaurus manselii, was first described by John Hulke in 1870.
facts.quote: The type species of Plesiosuchus, Steneosaurus manselii, was first described and named by John Hulke in 1870.

facts.statement: Richard Owen established the genus Plesiosuchus in 1884 because he believed the species was morphologically more similar to modern crocodilians than to Steneosaurus.
facts.quote: Richard Owen erected the genus Plesiosuchus for S. manselii in 1884 as he considered it to be more similar morphologically to extant crocodylians than to Steneosaurus.

facts.statement: The generic name Plesiosuchus combines the Greek word for 'near' with the Latinized name of the Egyptian crocodile god.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from plesios (πλεσιος), "near" or "close to" in Ancient Greek, and suchus (συχος) which is the Latinised form of the Ancient Greek word for the crocodile god of ancient Egypt.

facts.statement: The specific name manselii honors the discoverer John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell.
facts.quote: The specific name, manselii, honors it discoverer, John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell.

facts.statement: The type specimen and referred specimens were discovered by John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell in the 1860s along the Dorset coast alongside other large marine reptile remains.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo y los referidos a Plesiosuchus fueron descubiertos por John Clavell Mansel-Pleydell en la década de 1860 junto a los restos de otros grandes reptiles marinos a lo largo de la costa de Dorset.

facts.statement: Mansel-Pleydell donated these remains to the British Museum (now the Natural History Museum, London) in 1866.
facts.quote: Mansel-Pleydell entregó estos restos al Museo Británico (ahora en el Museo de Historia Natural de Londres) en 1866.

facts.statement: The holotype skull was initially thought to belong to a plesiosaur until preparator Mr Davies suggested it was crocodilian in nature.
facts.quote: Inicialmente, el cráneo (NHMUK PV OR40103) fue considerado de un pliosaurio; fue el preparador Mr Davies quien sugirió la naturaleza crocodiliana del cráneo.

facts.statement: In 1870, Hulke described the skull, which is preserved in two sections: the snout and the occiput.
facts.quote: En 1870, Hulke describió el cráneo, el cual está preservado en dos secciones: el rostro y el occipucio.

facts.statement: Hulke suggested the skull and lower jaw belonged to a single individual because they had the same dimensions and were found close together on an exposed reef in shallow waters at Kimmeridge Bay.
facts.quote: Hulke sugirió que "esta cabeza y la mandíbula inferior pertenecían a un solo individuo" ya que tenían las mismas dimensiones y fueron descubiertos en proximidad en un arrecife expuesto en aguas someras en Kimmeridge Bay.

facts.statement: The holotype represents a large individual, estimated at a total body length of 5.42 meters, though it is uncertain if it is an adult or subadult due to poor preservation of vertebral sutures.
facts.quote: El holotipo de Plesiosuchus representa un individuo grande. Si bien es incierto si el holotipo (y los especímenes referidos) pertenecen a adultos o subadultos debido a que ninguna de las vértebras están lo suficientemente bien preservadas para determinar la naturaleza de las suturas neurocentrales, se ha estimado su longitud total corporal en 5.42 metros.
